sentence: If the administrative department ___ (verify) the service records by Friday, the commissioner will issue the appointment orders.

steps.step1_marker: Clauses Identify Karein: Condition Clause = 'If the administrative department ___ the service records'. Result Clause = 'the commissioner will issue the appointment orders' (modal 'will + V1' use hua hai).
steps.step2_time: Temporal Alignment: Result clause future event ('will issue') ki baat kar raha hai jo reality mein possible hai.
steps.step3_aspect: Type Selection: Realistic future condition ke liye First Conditional (Type 1) rule lagu hota hai: 'If + Simple Present, will + V1'.
steps.step4_inflection: Verb Inflection: Subject 'the administrative department' 3rd person singular noun hai, isliye Simple Present mein base verb 'verify' ka 'verifies' banega.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'If the administrative department verifies the service records by Friday, the commissioner will issue the appointment orders.'

trapWarning: EXAM TRAP: 'Will verify' kabhi na chunein. English mein temporal aur conditional clauses ke andar future marker 'will' strictly prohibited hota hai.

sentence: If the prosecution ___ (present) the call detail records during trial, the bench would have convicted the conspirator.

steps.step1_marker: Clauses Identify Karein: Condition Clause = 'If the prosecution ___ the call detail records'. Result Clause = 'the bench would have convicted the conspirator' ('would have + V3').
steps.step2_time: Temporal Alignment: Result clause past ke finished unfulfilled action ('would have convicted') ko express karta hai jo trial ke waqt nahi hua.
steps.step3_aspect: Type Selection: Counterfactual unreal past condition ke liye Third Conditional (Type 3) formula lagta hai: 'If + Past Perfect (had + V3), would have + V3'.
steps.step4_inflection: Verb Inflection: Auxiliary 'had' + regular past participle V3 'presented' ➔ 'had presented'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'If the prosecution had presented the call detail records during trial, the bench would have convicted the conspirator.'

trapWarning: FATAL DISTRACTOR: 'Would have presented' option mein hamesha diya jata hai. If-clause mein 'would have' lagana fatal error hai; wahan strictly 'had + V3' lagta hai.

sentence: If the clerk ___ (be) more careful with document indexing, he would not misplace urgent writ petitions so frequently.

steps.step1_marker: Clauses Identify Karein: Condition Clause = 'If the clerk ___ more careful...'. Result Clause = 'he would not misplace urgent writ petitions' ('would + V1').
steps.step2_time: Temporal Alignment: Result clause present general habit/state ('misplace so frequently') par hypothetical comment kar raha hai.
steps.step3_aspect: Type Selection: Hypothetical present condition ke liye Second Conditional (Type 2) rule lagta hai: 'If + Simple Past / Subjunctive were, would + V1'.
steps.step4_inflection: Verb Inflection: Formal grammar aur competitive examinations mein imaginary/contrary-to-fact condition mein singular subject ('the clerk') ke sath bhi 'was' ki jagah subjunctive 'were' lagta hai.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'If the clerk were more careful with document indexing, he would not misplace urgent writ petitions so frequently.'

trapWarning: SUBJUNCTIVE TRAP: Option mein 'was' diya hoga. Informal speech mein log 'was' bol dete hain, lekin High Court exam mein contrary-to-fact clause mein strictly 'were' hi sahi answer hota hai.

sentence: Had the municipal authority ___ (issue) the statutory notice in advance, the demolition would not have been declared illegal.

steps.step1_marker: Structure Identify Karein: Sentence 'Had' se shuru ho raha hai bina 'if' ke: 'Had + the municipal authority + ___'. Result clause: 'would not have been declared' ('would have + V3').
steps.step2_time: Temporal Alignment: Beete huye past demolition action ki unfulfilled condition hai.
steps.step3_aspect: Type Selection: Ye Type 3 conditional ka formal inverted structure hai: 'Had + Subject + V3 ..., Subject + would have + V3'.
steps.step4_inflection: Verb Inflection: Auxiliary 'Had' already subject se pehle aa chuka hai, isliye blank mein main verb ka past participle V3 'issued' aayega.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'Had the municipal authority issued the statutory notice in advance, the demolition would not have been declared illegal.'

trapWarning: INVERSION TRAP: 'Had the authority issue' (V1) ya 'Had the authority would issue' bilkul galat hain. Had inversion mein main verb hamesha V3 (past participle) hoti hai.

sentence: If iron ___ (expose) to moist air over a period of time, it corrodes.

steps.step1_marker: Clauses Identify Karein: Condition Clause = 'If iron ___ to moist air'. Result Clause = 'it corrodes' (Simple Present V_s/es).
steps.step2_time: Temporal Alignment: Iron ka corrode hona ek permanent universal metallurgical aur chemical law hai.
steps.step3_aspect: Type Selection: Universal physical fact ke liye Zero Conditional (Type 0) rule lagta hai: dono clauses Simple Present mein rehte hain.
steps.step4_inflection: Voice & Inflection: Subject 'iron' khud action nahi karta balki us par action hota hai (passive voice). Simple Present passive = 'is exposed'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'If iron is exposed to moist air over a period of time, it corrodes.'

trapWarning: TENSE & VOICE TRAP: 'Will be exposed' ya 'was exposed' na chunein. Permanent scientific processes hamesha Simple Present mein express kiye jaate hain.

sentence: If the senior system assistant had migrated the database last month, our servers ___ (run) on the new Linux kernel today.

steps.step1_marker: Clauses Identify Karein: Condition Clause = 'If the senior system assistant had migrated the database last month' ('had + V3' with past marker 'last month'). Result Clause contains present time marker 'today'.
steps.step2_time: Temporal Alignment: Condition past ki unfulfilled event hai ('last month'), lekin result aaj present moment ka state hai ('today').
steps.step3_aspect: Type Selection: Ye Mixed Conditional hai (Type 3 Condition + Type 2 Result): 'If + Past Perfect, Subject + would + V1 (present)'.
steps.step4_inflection: Verb Inflection: Modal 'would' + base verb V1 'run' ➔ 'would run'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'If the senior system assistant had migrated the database last month, our servers would run on the new Linux kernel today.'

trapWarning: MIXED ADVERB TRAP: Candidates 'had migrated' dekhkar blindly 'would have run' laga dete hain. Lekin dhyan se dekhein: end mein 'today' likha hai! Isliye 'would run' correct hai.

sentence: Unless the petitioner ___ (furnish) the certified copy of the decree, the appeal will be dismissed at the threshold.

steps.step1_marker: Conjunction Identify Karein: Sentence 'Unless' se shuru ho raha hai ('Unless the petitioner ___'). Result clause = 'the appeal will be dismissed' (future passive).
steps.step2_time: Temporal Alignment: Future condition with realistic possibility.
steps.step3_aspect: Rule Selection: 'Unless' = 'If not'. Iske clause mein doosra negative word nahi aa sakta, aur tense Simple Present lagta hai (First Conditional logic).
steps.step4_inflection: Verb Inflection: 3rd person singular subject 'the petitioner' ke sath Simple Present affirmative V_s/es 'furnishes' aayega.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'Unless the petitioner furnishes the certified copy of the decree, the appeal will be dismissed at the threshold.'

trapWarning: DOUBLE NEGATIVE TRAP: 'Unless the petitioner does not furnish' bilkul galat option hai. 'Unless' already negative hai, isliye iske sath 'does not' kabhi nahi lagta.

sentence: Should you ___ (encounter) any technical difficulty during the computer typing test, raise your hand immediately.

steps.step1_marker: Structure Identify Karein: Sentence 'Should' se start ho raha hai: 'Should you ___ any technical difficulty...'. Result clause: 'raise your hand immediately' (Imperative instruction).
steps.step2_time: Temporal Alignment: Future realistic contingency ('if you happen to encounter').
steps.step3_aspect: Type Selection: Ye Type 1 conditional ki formal inversion hai: 'Should + Subject + V1 ..., Imperative / will + V1'.
steps.step4_inflection: Verb Inflection: Modal auxiliary 'Should' ke baad hamesha base verb V1 'encounter' aati hai.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'Should you encounter any technical difficulty during the computer typing test, raise your hand immediately.'

trapWarning: MEANING DISAMBIGUATION: Yahan 'Should' ka matlab 'chahiye' (duty) nahi hai, balki formal conditional 'if by chance' hai. Iske baad verb ki base form V1 hi aati hai.

sentence: Were the high court ___ (sanction) additional digital courtrooms, the trial backlog would decrease substantially.
tense: Were Inversion with Action Verb (Type 2 Inverted)

steps.step1_marker: Structure Identify Karein: Sentence 'Were' se shuru ho raha hai: 'Were the high court ___ additional digital courtrooms...'. Result clause: 'would decrease' ('would + V1').
steps.step3_aspect: Type Selection: Jab Type 2 conditional mein action verb ko 'Were' ke sath invert karte hain, toh structure banta hai: 'Were + Subject + to + V1 ..., would + V1'.
steps.step4_inflection: Verb Inflection: Inverted infinitive construction: 'to' + base verb 'sanction' ➔ 'to sanction'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'Were the high court to sanction additional digital courtrooms, the trial backlog would decrease substantially.'

trapWarning: INFINITIVE INVERSION TRAP: 'Were the high court sanctioned' (V2/V3) galat hai. Action verbs ke sath 'Were + Subject + to + V1' ka pattern lagta hai.

sentence: If I ___ (know) the legal provisions regarding contempt of court, I would explain them to the junior advocates now.

steps.step1_marker: Clauses Identify Karein: Condition Clause = 'If I ___ the legal provisions'. Result Clause = 'I would explain them to the junior advocates now' ('would + V1' with present adverb 'now').
steps.step2_time: Temporal Alignment: Reality ye hai ki speaker ko present mein provisions nahi pata ('I do not know right now').
steps.step3_aspect: Type Selection: Present hypothetical situation ke liye Second Conditional (Type 2) rule lagta hai: 'If + Simple Past (V2), would + V1'.
steps.step4_inflection: Verb Inflection: Irregular verb 'know' ka Simple Past V2 form 'knew' hota hai.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'If I knew the legal provisions regarding contempt of court, I would explain them to the junior advocates now.'

trapWarning: 'Had known' tab aata jab result mein 'would have explained' hota (past unreal). Result mein 'would explain' (V1) hai, isliye if-clause mein sirf 'knew' (V2) aayega.

sentence: If the forensic laboratory had processed the ballistics evidence faster, the police ___ (could / crack) the syndicate last year.

steps.step1_marker: Clauses Identify Karein: Condition Clause = 'If the forensic laboratory had processed...' ('had + V3' Past Perfect). Result Clause past time marker 'last year' contain karta hai.
steps.step2_time: Temporal Alignment: Past unreal condition aur past missed ability.
steps.step3_aspect: Type Selection: Third Conditional mein past capability/ability express karne ke liye 'could have + V3' lagta hai.
steps.step4_inflection: Verb Inflection: Modal 'could have' + past participle V3 'cracked'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'If the forensic laboratory had processed the ballistics evidence faster, the police could have cracked the syndicate last year.'

trapWarning: 'Could crack' (Type 2) na chunein kyunki baat past year ke finished event ki hai. Unreal past ability ke liye hamesha 'could have + V3' lagta hai.

sentence: Provided that the candidate ___ (possess) a valid RSCIT certificate, he is eligible for the System Assistant post.

steps.step1_marker: Conjunction Identify Karein: 'Provided that' (= on the condition that) se conditional clause shuru ho raha hai. Result: 'he is eligible' (Simple Present).
steps.step2_time: Temporal Alignment: Official eligibility rule jo general criterion ko define karta hai.
steps.step3_aspect: Rule Selection: 'Provided that' ke baad factual/standard rule ke liye Simple Present tense lagta hai.
steps.step4_inflection: Verb Inflection: Subject 'the candidate' singular hai, isliye verb 'possess' ka 'possesses' banega.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'Provided that the candidate possesses a valid RSCIT certificate, he is eligible for the System Assistant post.'

trapWarning: 'Provided that the candidate will possess' galat hai. Conditional conjunctions ke baad future 'will' use nahi hota.

sentence: If you require emergency leave for judicial duties, ___ (submit) an application to the District Judge directly.

steps.step1_marker: Clauses Identify Karein: Condition Clause = 'If you require emergency leave...' (Simple Present V1). Result Clause mein subject missing hai.
steps.step2_time: Temporal Alignment: Procedural instruction for future contingency.
steps.step3_aspect: Type Selection: Jab result clause direct instruction ya order hota hai, toh imperative mood use hota hai.
steps.step4_inflection: Verb Inflection: Imperative sentence base form V1 se shuru hota hai: 'submit'.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'If you require emergency leave for judicial duties, submit an application to the District Judge directly.'

trapWarning: Option mein 'you will submit' aur 'submitting' diye hote hain. Direct instruction ke liye standard base form 'submit' correct hai.

sentence: Had the defense counsel not ___ (object) to the hearsay testimony, the magistrate would have admitted it into evidence.

steps.step1_marker: Structure Identify Karein: Negative inverted construction: 'Had + Subject (the defense counsel) + not + ___'. Result clause: 'would have admitted'.
steps.step2_time: Temporal Alignment: Unreal past trial proceeding.
steps.step3_aspect: Type Selection: Type 3 negative inversion: 'Had + Subject + not + V3 ..., would have + V3'.
steps.step4_inflection: Verb Inflection: Blank 'not' ke baad hai, jahan main verb ka past participle V3 'objected' lagega.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'Had the defense counsel not objected to the hearsay testimony, the magistrate would have admitted it into evidence.'

trapWarning: WORD ORDER WARNING: Dhyan dein ki 'not' subject ke baad aaya hai ('Had the defense counsel not objected'). 'Had not the defense counsel objected' likhna modern standard exams mein error mana jata hai.

sentence: If you heat ice above zero degrees Celsius, it ___ (melt).

steps.step1_marker: Clauses Identify Karein: Condition Clause = 'If you heat ice above zero degrees Celsius' (Simple Present V1). Result Clause = 'it ___'.
steps.step2_time: Temporal Alignment: Barf ka 0°C se upar pighalna ek permanent physical necessity hai.
steps.step3_aspect: Type Selection: Factual physical reality ke liye Zero Conditional (Type 0) rule lagta hai: Simple Present + Simple Present.
steps.step4_inflection: Verb Inflection: Subject 'it' 3rd person singular hai, isliye Simple Present verb 'melt' ka 'melts' banega.
steps.step5_synthesis: Final Output: 'If you heat ice above zero degrees Celsius, it melts.'

trapWarning: RESULT CLAUSE OVER-COMPLICATION: 'It will melt' ya 'it would melt' options galat hain. Permanent physical facts hamesha Simple Present 'melts' mein hi likhe jaate hain.
